title: Stress scenario microdrills and KPI bakeoff
content:
Purpose: quick, runnable list of small-scale (15-90m) launch microdrills to validate KPIs and operational playbooks before phased rollout. This is intentionally tactical: short drill, clear SLOs, observable signals, rapid retro.

Summary: why this doc exists
- Reduce uncertainty for first 24–72 hours after activation by rehearsing high-risk failure modes in controlled windows.
- Treat each microdrill like an experiment: define hypothesis, success metrics, runbook steps, rollback triggers, and owner.

Sheet layout (tab simulation):
- Drill name | Hypothesis | Inputs (traffic, payload mix) | KPIs to watch | Observability hooks | Playbook steps (1..n) | Escalation owner | Dry-run window | Acceptance criteria | Postmortem owner

Example drills (concise):
1) Cold-cache storm (15m): hypothesis = prefix KV cache miss spikes tail-latency > 200ms for p95. Inputs = 3k short requests/min with varied prompt lengths. KPIs = p50/p95 latency, token cost, error-rate. Obs = per-model p95, batching queue length, GPU util. Steps = warm up small steady baseline; switch traffic; observe 15m; run fallback to smaller model variant if p95 > 300ms for 5m. Owner = eng-serving-runtime. Acceptance = p95 < 250ms or graceful fallback without user error surfacing.

2) Batching collapse (30m): hypothesis = sudden skewed seq-length causes batching to fall back to single-token steps increasing cost by >40%. Inputs = 1:10 ratio long prompts. KPIs = tokens/sec, average batch size, per-token cost delta. Playbook = enable emergency quantized variant, adjust batching-window TTL, monitor cache hit. Rollback trigger = sustained cost delta > 30% for 10m. Owner = infra-performance.

3) Canary degradation with partial model fallback (45m): hypothesis = model A regresses on hallucination metric > threshold when traffic increases. Inputs = canary ramp 0->10% in 20m. KPIs = hallucination-rate (eval prompts), answer-quality score (sampled), latency. Playbook = automatic rollback to model B at 10% regressing or manual pause. Owner = product-hosted-api. Acceptance = no quality regression beyond 2% absolute vs baseline.

Run logistics checklist:
- Pre-run: confirm dry-run dataset and synthetic generator (link to generator script), obs dashboards ready, on-call notified, post-run retro slot reserved.
- Decision owner: product-ops lead for go/no-go.
- Communications: Slack #launch-ops ping, brief template with real-time KPIs.

Observability quick hits:
- Required dashboards: per-route latency tile, token-cost burn, model-quality sampler, batch-size distribution.
- Trace-level hooks: sample request ids + kv-cache state, GPU mem pressure snapshots.

Post-run postmortem template (short):
- What happened (one-liner)
- Hypothesis confirmed? yes/no + evidence
- KPIs: baseline vs run (p50/p95, cost, error-rate)
- Action items (owner + due date)
- Followups: larger-scale rehearsal needed?

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Do we have automated synthetic generators for embeddings-heavy workloads (owner: applied-ml)?
- Should rollback to region-level or model-variant-level be the default for Dedicated customers? (ops/legal flagged)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep drills 15-90m max, prefer multiple back-to-back small experiments over one large stress test.
- Paper-provision a small standby pool of GPU capacity for dry-runs to avoid impacting prod.
- Validate alert thresholds once per quarter as model and infra change.

Attachments/links: generator script (github PR above), local dry-run calendar template, short slide deck with visualization of typical failure-mode curves (link internal).

Quick actionables for next 30d:
- Assign owners for missing observability hooks (Jamal)
- Build small synthetic embedding generator (Samir)
- Schedule 3 microdrills ahead of pilot (Elena)

Status: draft checklist + experiment matrix; aiming to convert to formal runbook after 3 successful microdrills and one cross-team exercise.

Editors: Mira (author), Jamal/Elena/Samir reviewers.
